solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Uproar after losing current leader of South Africa in disorder

indicators.note: letters in disorder are jumbled, so the pieces before it are to be rearranged
losing says a letter is dropped from the country's name

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from South

explanation.surface: A news report: after a power cut, chaos breaks out in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops I from AFRICA, and 'in disorder' rearranges the remaining AFRCA; the S from 'leader of South' ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or brawl, a close synonym of uproar.

clue.text: Error made by football manager last month

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, is the body that runs English football
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A football manager blundered last month, and the papers say so.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is the governing body of English football, playfully called its manager here.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault is a mistake or flaw, a straightforward synonym of error.

clue.text: State of several articles punctuated by large black marks

parts.note: A is the indefinite article; several of them give four A's
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
M stands for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A newspaper so full of black blots that its articles are hard to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punctuated by' says L, B and M break up the run of four A's one at a time, giving A-L-A-B-A-M-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty US states, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Decoration comprising a small circle worn by members of Royal Navy?

indicators.note: something worn by people sits on or around them, so the circle's letters wrap the sailors

parts.note: a dot is a tiny round mark
members of a crew are its men

explanation.surface: A medal: a little round badge pinned on sailors of the Royal Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' reads as the sailors wearing the dot, but the dot's letters wrap round them, split after DO.
explanation.definitionFit: An adornment is an ornament or embellishment, so it is a kind of decoration.

clue.text: Thing that has old man embracing old boy in greeting

indicators.note: embracing means the father's letters wrap around everything else

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: in places the old boy's letters inside the greeting

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A father hugging a former schoolboy while saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thing' is the informal sense in 'she has a thing about spiders'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something means an irrational fear or obsession, which is what a phobia is.

clue.text: What's used to raise army to protect Italy

indicators.note: to protect something you surround it, so the army's letters enclose the country's

parts.note: a host is an archaic word for an army
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A question of how troops are raised to defend Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' looks like recruiting the army, but the definition means lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a lifting device, a pulley or crane for heavy loads.

clue.text: Fare from Mexico City's centre charges the earth almost

indicators.note: charges here means rushes in, so the city's centre enters the den
almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an earth is a fox's den, a burrow

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here of City

explanation.surface: Prices in central Mexico City are sky-high, a travel complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BURROW to BURRO, and 'charges' sends IT, the middle of City, into it. An earth is a fox's den.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish of a tortilla wrapped round a filling, so it is food from Mexico.

clue.text: Rallied American behind me, turned and ran

parts.note: ass is the American word for the backside

indicators.note: turned means the word me is read backwards

parts.note: dye that ran has bled

explanation.surface: A soldier spins round and flees, with an American close behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives EM. A colour that runs in the wash is said to bleed.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops that rallied gathered together again, so they assembled.

clue.text: Person arranging work schedule policemen once backed

indicators.note: backed means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a rota is a list of who works when
the RUC, the Royal Ulster Constabulary, was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001

explanation.surface: A former police force supports someone drawing up the duty roster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ROTARUC round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator selects and lays out the items in an exhibition or collection.

clue.text: Writer is tense after counter-attack

indicators.note: after places is tense behind the reversed attack
counter means going against, so the attack is read backwards

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A writer grows nervous after a military counter-attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-attack' looks like one military word; 'counter' is turning RAID into DIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist is someone who writes a diary, so a particular kind of writer.

clue.text: Bias in operation is intimidating

parts.note: a leaning is a bias or inclination
a machine in operation is on

explanation.surface: A complaint that a prejudiced procedure is bullying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' belongs to the definition: 'is leaning on' someone means pressuring them.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning on someone is an idiom for pressuring or threatening them.

clue.text: Case of apparent corruption involving staff acquisition

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, first and last letters
involving means the corruption's letters wrap round the staff

parts.note: taint is moral corruption
a staff of workers are its men

explanation.surface: A corruption scandal involving employees over a company purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a stick, but it is the workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is something gained or achieved, which matches an acquisition.

clue.text: Bit of poetry penned by William Blake

indicators.note: penned by means the letters are enclosed within the poet's name

explanation.surface: A line of verse written by the poet William Blake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like authorship, but the answer is enclosed in the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot, an unstressed then stressed syllable, a small unit of verse.

clue.text: Work of author concealed end of novel in daring neologism

parts.note: brave means daring

indicators.note: concealed means the novel's last letter is hidden inside the neologism's letters

parts.note: a neologism is literally a new word

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of novel

explanation.surface: An author's daring coinage hidden at the end of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' puts L inside NEW WORD. Brave New World is Aldous Huxley's dystopian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave New World is a 1932 novel by Aldous Huxley, so a literary work by one writer.

clue.text: Complain beautiful woman has commandeered vessel briefly

indicators.note: a vessel commandeered is taken inside the woman's control, so her letters enclose it

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a yacht is a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A beauty seizes a boat for a while and someone grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' here trims the boat word by its last letter rather than meaning 'for a short time'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellyache is an informal idiom for grumbling or whining.

clue.text: See 13
Spooner's only greeting is indiscriminate

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade their first sounds

parts.note: sole means only
hail is a greeting

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner's one salutation is careless.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLE HAIL with first sounds swapped gives HOLE SALE, said as WHOLE SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale means on a vast, undiscriminating scale, as in wholesale slaughter.

clue.text: School dinners comprising tiny portions in the main?

definitions.text: School dinners comprising tiny portions in the main?

parts.words: School dinners comprising tiny portions in the main?
parts.note: a school is a group of fish or whales, and the main is the sea, so this is the minute food eaten there

explanation.surface: A grumble about meagre school lunches, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests a classroom, but it is a shoal of sea creatures; 'in the main' sounds like 'mostly', but means 'in the ocean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms drifting in the sea that many fish and whales feed on.

clue.text: Hotel abandons seemingly spartan floor

indicators.note: abandons means a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: seemingly flags a made-up word: spartan would be non-plush
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel leaves a bare floor that looks austere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is the verb, meaning to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to leave them baffled and lost for words, which is to nonplus them.

clue.text: American got rid of following pages in dictionary

indicators.note: in places the pages' letters inside the dictionary

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
ff. is the abbreviation for following pages in references

explanation.surface: An American discards the later pages of a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got rid of' looks like plain discarding, but OFFED is US slang for killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To off someone is American slang for to kill them, so offed is past tense.

clue.text: Whistleblower recalled being filled with desire to cause embarrassment

indicators.note: being filled with means the reversed official's letters go round the desire
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a referee, ref for short, blows the whistle in a match
lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: A whistleblower, called back and full of longing, embarrasses everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' suggests an informer; it is a referee. 'recalled' gives FER, which 'being filled with' wraps round LUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluster someone is to make them agitated and confused, which is causing embarrassment.

clue.text: Song that man heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is spoken, so its sound is used

parts.note: him refers to that man

explanation.surface: A song that someone overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: HIM and HYMN are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise.

clue.text: Lawyer's writing ignored body of work

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly

indicators.note: the body of a word is its middle, the letters between its ends

explanation.surface: A lawyer's prose overlooked a whole body of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body of work' looks like an oeuvre; 'body of' takes OR, the middle of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor is the lawyer who brings a criminal case against a defendant.

clue.text: Substitute player who's paid by year

parts.note: a pro is a professional player, paid to play
x is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: A stand-in professional paid on an annual contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is the times sign, as in a room 3 x 4 metres.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is someone authorised to act for another, a substitute.

clue.text: Sanctions really limiting pointless dialogue after revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution something is turned round, so the result is read backwards
limiting means the first word's letters enclose the second's

parts.note: so means really, as in 'so good'
yak is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Tough sanctions curbing futile talks after a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' turns the whole SYAKO round. 'Sanctions' is the verb, meaning approves, not penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to approve it, and okays means approves.

clue.text: Shell's concession involving summons

indicators.note: involving means the concession's letters surround the summons

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone
a call is a summons

explanation.surface: An oil company's concession over a court summons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' suggests the oil company; it is a seashell.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a bivalve mollusc, and also its fan-shaped shell.

clue.text: What is true, notwithstanding a bit of fiction?

definitions.text: What is true, notwithstanding a bit of fiction?

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here its first letter, from fiction

parts.note: actual means real or true

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether something is true despite a dash of invention.
explanation.walkthrough: F, the first of fiction, goes before ACTUAL; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual means based on facts, so it describes what is true.

clue.text: State blocks 60% of press articles

indicators.note: the stated word blocks the gap, sitting inside the remaining letters
60% of a five-letter word is its last three letters, the tail of press

parts.note: taken as written
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A government blocks most press reports.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of' leaves ESS of press; 'blocks' puts SAY inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Essays are short written pieces, the sort printed as articles.

clue.text: Refuse to reduce debt and risk

indicators.note: to reduce each word, its last letter is cut away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sensible plan to cut borrowing and danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reduce' removes the last letter of each word: DEB and RIS. 'Refuse' is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or waste, the noun sense of refuse.
